answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy must price identity, not just count it. When each agent earns only after its work is verified by independent peers and its stake is slashed on fraud, a saffron flood of fake accounts buys nothing: every new identity needs locked collateral, a history of useful attestations, and time. Crystal-clear reputation makes cheap copies visible, because a fresh account cannot fake a sonnet of consistent, costly, cross-checked contributions. The attacker pays full price for every fake while the network pays only for verified value.
